text: Rat-Trap Bond Masonry is a simple yet effective brick-laying technique that uses fewer materials without compromising strength.

candidates.what: After a ~0.4 s near-static start, the camera tracks and pans smoothly leftward along a cream-painted brick exhibition wall, moving past framed instructional posters starting with 'Compressed Earth Blocks', 'Rat Trap Bond', and 'Arch Foundation', then continuing past 'Appropriate technologies', 'Cleanliness in Lavatory & Bathroom', 'Kitchen and Bedroom', and 'Living Room' toward the room corner.
candidates.why: the 'Rat Trap Bond' poster summarizes 'Has equal strength as other bonds' and 'Stability of wall is not affected' alongside brick savings, illustrating the concept on a display board.
candidates.missing: shows an informational poster rather than real-world rat-trap bond brick-laying or structural testing.

candidates.what: With his head completely above the top frame edge, the foreground mason lays five consecutive red bricks on edge in the alternating Rat-Trap Bond pattern: first placing a transverse header brick on edge across the wall width (26.3-28.8 s), then two parallel longitudinal stretcher bricks on edge behind/alongside it (29.4-32.6 s and 33.2-36.0 s), followed by two more longitudinal stretcher bricks on edge (36.4-39.5 s and 40.2-42.6 s), visibly enclosing rectangular hollow cavities inside the wall.
